clue.text: Not all members of cast go their own way

parts.note: not all of something is only a part of it
the members of a theatrical cast together form the company

explanation.surface: Some of the actors in a production walk out and go separate ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Not all members of cast' as two pieces: 'Not all' is a part, and the members of a cast are its company.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up and take separate paths is an idiom for ending an association, as people do when they separate.

clue.text: Reports on sailors by leading chartists

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: reports are loud bangs, or pops
tars is an old word for sailors

explanation.surface: News reports about sailors, written by the top people in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue placing: the bangs (reports) sit above the sailors. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Successful singers who top the record charts are the leading chartists; 'chartist' is used playfully for a chart act.

clue.text: Take cover again in check? Of course

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain, as with a horse
sure is a casual way of saying of course

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to renew an insurance policy that is being checked, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' points to insurance, so taking cover again means renewing it; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is called cover, so insuring once more is taking cover again.

clue.text: Hundreds in deep sleep used to break up sentence

indicators.note: the numeral is placed in the word for a deep sleep

parts.note: a coma is a deep, prolonged unconsciousness
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, ten hundreds

explanation.surface: A huge number of people in a deep sleep helps to break up a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside COMA. The clue prints 'Hundreds', but M is the Roman numeral for a thousand; only M gives the answer, so the clue has a slip. 'sentence' suggests prison but means a grammatical sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark is placed to divide a written sentence into parts.

clue.text: Skip with air! abrnad

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Skip with air! abrnad (4,3)': garbled OCR; 'Skip' defines MISS OUT and 'abroad' probably gives OUT, but the word giving MISS is lost

clue.text: Assistant to a punter

parts.note: a punter is someone who places bets, a better

explanation.surface: A helper working for a gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. Abettor is the legal spelling, but abetter is also used for one who assists.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abets is a helper or accomplice, an assistant in some act.

clue.text: Crime squad's instant standard

parts.note: the Yard (Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters) with its 's gives the possessive
a tick is a moment or instant, as in 'back in a tick'

explanation.surface: The police squad's immediate benchmark for judging cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, often called just 'the Yard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring rod a yard long gives its name to any measure or criterion used for comparison.

clue.text: Due to 12th man

definitions.meaning: a subscription or membership fee, a due paid
the twelfth man in cricket is the substitute fielder

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. In cricket a team has eleven players, and the twelfth man is the reserve who fields as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription is a regular payment owed, and a substitute is the player who comes on in place of another.

clue.text: Calm down sweetheart

definitions.meaning: to make or become calm and stable

explanation.definitionFit: To steady is to settle or calm, and a steady is a regular romantic partner.

clue.text: Harry the beast

definitions.meaning: to harry is to pester or harass persistently
a nocturnal burrowing mammal with a striped face

explanation.definitionFit: To pester is to harass someone, and the striped burrowing mammal is a familiar woodland animal.

clue.text: Trojan handling public relations one morning

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A man from Troy works in PR one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handling' is a link word. 'Trojan' is a person from Troy here, not a hard worker or a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the king of Troy during the Trojan War in Greek legend.

clue.text: Attack leader with lance in the end

parts.note: a lance is a long spear
a head is one end of something, as the head of a table

explanation.surface: The man leading the charge carries a lance with a point at its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'in the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front of an assault, or the person at its front, leads the attack.

clue.text: Cast prepared to have restless night in bed

parts.note: to cast is to throw or toss
about to means ready or prepared to do something

explanation.surface: Actors ready to lie awake all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a group of actors, but it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash around sleeplessly is to turn over again and again under the covers.

clue.text: Plant showing old Bob to advantage

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s
an edge is an advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A plant shows Bob, an old man, at his best.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was slang for a shilling in pre-decimal British money, written s. 'showing' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-like plant growing in wet ground is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Underdone part of dish

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A lightly cooked piece of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese melted on toast is a savoury dish.

clue.text: Stop offer being made to pump handler

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop making an offer to the man working a pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being made to' are link words. The beer pump in a pub is worked by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person serving drinks pulls beer from the handpump at the bar.

clue.text: Soldiers I would use for invasion

parts.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery, a regiment of soldiers
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Soldiers saying they would use force to invade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden incursion into enemy territory is a small-scale invasion.

clue.text: Fashionable position taken up in illustration

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A trendy pose adopted in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An example given to make a point clear illustrates it.

clue.text: Entire range of truce MPs re-write

indicators.note: rewriting the words truce and MPs puts their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Every member of parliament redrafts the truce.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-write' reorders TRUCE and MPS. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A full span of values or opinions is the whole range from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Germany beginning to free network

indicators.note: the beginning of the word Germany is its first letter

parts.note: to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Germany starting to free up its network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. The National Grid is Britain's electricity network.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of crossing lines, or a power distribution system, forms a network.

clue.text: Garment fitting chest

definitions.meaning: the sliding boxes fitted into a chest of ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both underpants and the sliding compartments of a piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Shortened while occupied

definitions.meaning: a hem raised to shorten a garment
busy or filled, as time ... by work

explanation.walkthrough: 'while' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt raised at the hem is shortened, and time filled by a task is occupied.

clue.text: Gossip columnist on magazine we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us a word is said out loud and spelt another way

parts.note: Tatler is a British society magazine

explanation.surface: A gossip writer working on a magazine, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatler is a British society and fashion magazine. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale who spreads rumours is a gossip, the stock in trade of a gossip writer.

clue.text: Swears at article on public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, the article placed on top comes first

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
buses are public transport

explanation.surface: Someone curses at a newspaper article about buses.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult someone with foul language is to verbally mistreat them.

clue.text: Just exclude cathedral

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Simply keep someone out of the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a small city near Cambridge, is famous for its cathedral; in crosswords 'cathedral' or 'see' often gives ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just, by a narrow margin, is the sense of 'just' here.

clue.text: Indian the railways welcome

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railways
ave is a Latin greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A Native American warrior welcomed by the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior of a Native American people was called a brave.

clue.text: Aim to cut a faulty weapon

indicators.note: something faulty is out of order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying to slash a gun that keeps jamming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges AIM TO CUT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm that reloads and fires continuously is an automatic weapon.

clue.text: First person to shelter in scrum

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun
the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: Being the first to take cover during a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. 'scrum' here is a confused crowd, not a rugby set piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly crush of people is a confused fight or crowd.

clue.text: Blooming specimen gond wishes to racing driver

definitions.meaning: the words one says to wish a racing driver well: go fast and do it well

explanation.definitionFit: The small blue-flowered plant takes a name that reads as a wish for fast and successful going.

clue.text: Family right to go by boat

parts.note: a line is a family lineage

explanation.surface: A family entitled to travel by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger ship sailing a regular route is an ocean liner.

clue.text: Express for instance

explanation.definitionFit: To voice a thought is to state it, and the word also introduces an example.

clue.text: Put by 11 seconds

parts.note: to reserve something is to put it by for later
eleven players make up a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: Eleven seconds set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like time, but means a second string of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's second string of players, below the first eleven, are its seconds.
